title: The parent and child never let go
summary: A reference cycle keeps the count off zero. The back edge becomes a weak_ptr read through lock.

turns.user: dropping the scene root destroys nothing. not one child destructor runs. these ARE shared_ptr

assistant.body: Great question. The parent holds the children and each child holds the parent, so both counts sit at one forever. Let only one direction own, and make the back edge a weak_ptr. attach itself keeps working.

turns.user: destructors run now. but every node->parent->name site is broken. you said it keeps working?

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was not accurate. The assignment inside attach compiles, but weak_ptr has no operator->, so the reading sites are still broken. Promote it with lock() and check that the parent is alive before touching it.

turns.user: these type names are too long now. add aliases and rewrite them all. name the weak one too

assistant.body: The aliases go in at the top, then the long spellings get substituted in one pass. Node only needs a forward declaration to sit inside shared_ptr, so it can go above the struct. The & on the right of a substitution means the whole match, so it has to be escaped.

sed -i '' 's/^struct Node {/struct Node;\
using NodePtr = std::shared_ptr<Node>;\
using NodeRef = std::weak_ptr<Node>;\
\
struct Node {/; s/std::weak_ptr<Node> parent;/NodeRef parent;/; s/std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Node>>/std::vector<NodePtr>/; s/const std::shared_ptr<Node>\&/const NodePtr\&/g' src/scene/node.h
Ownership now points one way only. The edge that breaks a cycle is always the edge that does not own.
